title: Triage the Inbox from the keyboard, with snooze
subtitle: Move, act and snooze without the mouse; the same by touch on a phone. Pick one proposal per decision.

decisions.name: Moving through the Inbox
decisions.question: How does a person move through the Inbox and open an item from the keyboard, and how are the keys shown?
decisions.common: The Inbox as built: Needs you with its count, the New, Seen, Staged, Declined and Done tabs, rows by kind with each feature's code and name. j and k (or the arrow keys) move; nothing changes for a person who only clicks; the rail's Inbox count and the panel's count stay the same number.

proposals.name: Focused row, keys on buttons
proposals.what: The first key press marks a row with a blue edge. j and k move it; Enter opens the item right under its row (a question's answer box, a cost's reason) with Esc to close. Only the focused row shows its keys, as small key caps on its own buttons; a Keys button in the panel head (or ?) lists them all.
proposals.why: It adds the least to the page as built: rows, buttons and the open-in-place answer box already exist, the keys only show where they act, and a person who never touches the keyboard sees no change.
proposals.plus: The keys sit on the buttons they press, so nothing has to be learned up front; at rest each row gains only a snooze button (a moon) and the panel head a Keys button. Works the same in Simple and Detailed.
proposals.cost: 4 keys (j j j Enter) to open the fourth item, against today's scroll, find the row and 1 click.

frames.caption: At rest: the Inbox as it is today, plus a Keys button in the panel head and a snooze button (moon) on every row. No row is marked until a key is pressed.
j marks the first row; ? opens the list of keys beside the Keys button.
j j j: the blue edge is on the question from Teo; its Answer button shows Enter and its snooze button carries s.
Enter: the question opens under its row with its answer box; the other rows stay where they were. The note at the top counts the keys.
Detailed at 1512 with 47 items and long names: after 22 presses the marked row stays in view as the list scrolls.

A commenter at 1512: Needs you holds only what they can act on (questions, feedback, review reminders); feedback says Propose, as their change goes to the owners. Another role's items sit under For your information.
A viewer at 1512: Needs you holds only review reminders to read; the rest sits under For your information, which says once that they can read and owners decide.
Phone 390: no key caps and no Keys button; rows stack and keep their buttons for touch.

proposals.name: Reading pane
proposals.what: The list narrows to the left and the focused item reads in full on the right, like a mail app. j and k change what the pane shows at once; the pane has its own up and down buttons with k and j on them, and the item's actions with their keys. On a phone, tapping a row opens the item as a full sheet.
proposals.plus: An item can be read and settled without opening anything; good for long items and questions.
proposals.cost: 3 keys (j j j) and the item is already open, against today's scroll, 1 click and Back.

frames.caption: At rest: the list on the left with its first item open on the right, "1 of 14" above it.
j j j: the pane follows to the question from Teo, the answer box ready.
Typing the answer in the pane, the list unchanged.
Enter sends it: "Answered" with Undo, the counts drop to 16 and the pane moves to the next item.
Detailed at 1512 with 44 items and long names: the long question wraps in the pane; the list keeps its own scroll.
Phone 390: tapping a row opens it as a full sheet with its actions.

proposals.name: Tick and act together
proposals.what: Each row gets a tick box. j and k move, x ticks the focused row; a bar opens above the list with the number ticked and Accept a, Decline d, Snooze s, Clear Esc, which act on every ticked row at once.
proposals.plus: Fast for a pile of the same kind (many date suggestions); one action and one Undo for all.
proposals.cost: 13 keys for 3 items (j six times to the first, then x, j j x, j x, then a), against 3 clicks that each wait for their banner.

frames.caption: At rest: a tick box at the start of every row.
x on F-44 Smart oven timers: "1 ticked" bar opens with its actions and keys.
Two more ticked (F-47 Checkout totals, F-48 Leftovers planner): "3 ticked".
a: "3 items accepted" with Undo; they leave New for Staged and every count drops by 3.
1512 with 47 items: 14 ticked down the list; the "14 ticked" bar stays at the top on a solid strip and the rows scroll under it whole.
Phone 390: tick boxes by touch; the "3 ticked" bar sits on a solid strip above the tab bar with Accept, Decline, Snooze and Clear, no key caps; the list ends above it.

decisions.name: Acting from the keyboard
decisions.question: What do the action keys do, how does a person see the result, and how is it undone?
decisions.common: Uses the focused row from Moving through the Inbox. Each key does what the row's own button does and only what the person's role allows; another role's items sit under For your information, where "Owners decide" is said once; a commenter's change goes to the owners as a proposal. Every count (tabs, Needs you, the rail) changes at once. One Undo, for the last action, with z.

proposals.name: Act at once, one Undo
proposals.what: a accepts or approves, d declines, w keeps it in Seen, e marks it done, s snoozes. The row leaves at once, the focus moves to the next row, and the banner the Inbox already has says what happened with Undo (z).
proposals.why: It keeps the Inbox's own banner and Undo, costs one key, and the role rules already drawn on each row decide what a key may do.
proposals.plus: One key per item; the result and its Undo show in the place they show today.
proposals.cost: 1 key (a) per item and the focus is already on the next one, against find the button, 1 click, find the next row.

frames.caption: At rest: the cost approval is focused; its buttons show a and d, its snooze button s.
Enter opens it in place: the reason, with Move to Seen w and Done e beside it.
Esc, then a: "Approved: run started" with Undo z; the row is gone, the focus is on F-41 Recipe cards and Needs you, New and the rail drop by one.
z: "Undone"; the cost approval is back where it was, focused again, and every count is back.
A commenter at 1512: a on F-47 Checkout totals proposes it: "Sent to the owners as a proposal" with Undo. Owner-only items sit under For your information, "Owners decide" said once.
A viewer at 1512: only the review reminders can be acted on (Review opens them); everything else is under For your information.
Phone 390: tapping Approve does the same; the banner with Undo shows above the rows, no key caps.

proposals.name: Mark, then apply
proposals.what: Keys only mark rows and move on: the row's own button (Approve, Accept, Decline) is outlined, or a Done or To Seen chip shows. Nothing happens until Apply (Shift+Enter) in a bar at the foot of the list, which settles them together with one Undo.
proposals.plus: Room to change one's mind before anything happens; a batch reads as a plan.
proposals.cost: 6 keys for 4 items (a d e j w, then Shift+Enter), against 4 clicks with no way to settle them together.

frames.caption: At rest: the cost approval is focused with its keys.
a: the cost approval's own Approve button is outlined and the row stays; a bar opens at the foot: "1 marked", Apply.
d, e, then w on the next rows: "4 marked: 1 to approve, 1 decline, 1 done, 1 to seen".
Shift+Enter: "1 approved · 1 declined · 1 done · 1 moved to Seen" with Undo; the four rows leave New (one to Seen) and every count changes at once.

A commenter at 1512: F-47 Checkout totals feedback marked Propose and a question marked Done; the bar says "1 to propose · 1 done". Owner-only items sit under For your information and cannot be marked.
Phone 390: taps mark rows the same way (Approve and Accept outlined); the Apply bar sits above the tab bar with "2 marked".

proposals.name: One key opens the actions
proposals.what: Space (or .) opens a small menu at the focused row that lists only what this person can do here, each with its key. The result shows in the banner the Inbox already has, above the rows, with Undo.
proposals.plus: Nothing to remember: the menu says every action, and a commenter sees only theirs.

frames.caption: At rest: the focused row shows its main button and a menu button with Space.
Space: the menu lists Approve a, Decline d, Move to Seen w, Done e, Snooze s.
a: the banner above the rows says "Approved: run started" with Undo; the row is gone and the counts drop by one.
Undo in the banner: the cost approval is back and the counts are back.
A commenter at 1512: on F-47 Checkout totals the menu lists Propose, Decline, Move to Seen, Done and Snooze; owner-only items are under For your information.
Phone 390: each row keeps its main button and a ••• button; tapping ••• on Start run opens the same actions menu as Space: Approve, Decline, Move to Seen, Done, Snooze.

decisions.name: Snooze
decisions.question: Until when can an item be snoozed, where does it wait, how does it come back, and how is it done by touch?
decisions.common: Snoozing takes the item out of the list and out of every count until its time; it comes back into New at 9:00 AM on the day (or at the time picked) and says it is back. Dates read month first. On a phone the same choices open by touch. A commenter or viewer snoozes only what is in their own Needs you.

proposals.name: Four times, a Snoozed tab
proposals.what: s opens a short menu at the row: Later today 5:00 PM, Tomorrow 9:00 AM, Next week Mon 9:00 AM, Pick a day (keys 1 to 4). Snoozed items wait in their own Snoozed tab with when each comes back and Bring back now; back in New they carry "Back from snooze".
proposals.why: It keeps snoozed items in plain sight in a tab like the other states, offers the times people use most at one key each, and needs nothing new on a phone beyond a sheet.
proposals.plus: Every snoozed item can be found and woken by hand; matches the Inbox's state tabs.
proposals.cost: 3 keys for a day (s, 4, 1) or 2 for tomorrow (s, 2), against today: not possible, the item stays and is counted.

frames.caption: At rest: F-47 Checkout totals is focused; 2 items already wait in the Snoozed tab.
s: the menu shows Later today, Tomorrow, Next week and Pick a day, with 1 to 4; the snooze button is a moon, not the Dates clock.
4: ten days to pick from, each with its key.
1 (Wed Nov 25): F-47 Checkout totals leaves New, every count drops by one, Snoozed is 3; the Snoozed tab shows each item with when it comes back.
The next morning (Nov 25) at 1512 with long names: F-47 Checkout totals and F-35 Weekly menu email are back at the top of New with "Back from snooze · Nov 25"; Snoozed is 1.
Phone 390: the moon on F-47 Checkout totals opens a sheet named for it with the same four choices.
Phone 390: Tomorrow tapped: "F-47 Checkout totals snoozed: back Nov 25, 9:00 AM" with Undo; the tabs wrap so Snoozed 3 shows; New and Needs you drop by one.
A commenter at 1512: s on F-47 Checkout totals opens the same menu; only their own items can be snoozed.
A viewer at 1512: the review reminders can be snoozed; the rest is under For your information.

proposals.name: Tomorrow in one key
proposals.what: s snoozes until tomorrow 9:00 AM at once; Shift+s opens the day picker. Snoozed items wait in a "Snoozed" fold at the head of New, under the counts, rather than a tab. On a phone, a swipe left on a row shows Tomorrow (with its date) and Pick a day.
proposals.plus: The commonest case costs one key; no new tab.
proposals.cost: 1 key (s) for tomorrow, 2 for a day, against today: not possible.

frames.caption: At rest: F-47 Checkout totals is focused; a "Snoozed 2" fold sits at the head of the list.
Shift+s: the day picker for another day.
Esc, then s: "F-47 Checkout totals snoozed: back Nov 25, 9:00 AM" with Undo; the row is gone, Needs you and New drop by one, the fold says 3.
Opening the fold: the 3 snoozed items with their kind, when each comes back and Bring back now, the counts still in view.
The next morning (Nov 25) at 1512: F-47 Checkout totals and F-35 Weekly menu email are back at the top with "Back from snooze · Nov 25"; the fold above them says 1.
Phone 390: a swipe left on F-47 Checkout totals shows Tomorrow (Wed Nov 25) and Pick a day; its code and name stay readable.
Phone 390: Tomorrow tapped: "F-47 Checkout totals snoozed: back Nov 25, 9:00 AM" with Undo above the rows; New and Needs you drop by one, the fold says 3.

proposals.name: Until something happens
proposals.what: s opens a menu with times and events: Later today, Tomorrow, Next week, Until Product sync (the next meeting), Until the person replies, Until the run moves, and Pick a day. Snoozed items wait at the foot of Seen under "Coming back", each with one return label ("Back Nov 25, 9:00 AM", "Back after Product sync, Nov 26").
proposals.plus: Items come back when they can be acted on, not on a guessed date.
proposals.cost: 5 keys (s, down three times, Enter), against today: not possible.

frames.caption: At rest: F-47 Checkout totals is focused.
s: the menu offers Later today, Tomorrow, Next week, Until Product sync, Until Mara replies and Pick a day.
Down three times: Until Product sync, Thu Nov 26 is picked.
Enter, then Seen: "F-47 Checkout totals snoozed: back after Product sync, Nov 26"; under Coming back, each item with its kind, when it comes back and Bring back now.
A cost approval at 1512: the menu adds "Until the run moves"; each item gets the events that fit it.

After Product sync (Nov 26) at 1512: the snoozed items are back at the top of New, each chip saying why: F-47 Checkout totals and F-33 Printable lists after Product sync, F-35 Weekly menu email since Nov 25.
Phone 390: the same menu as a sheet from the moon on the row.
Phone 390: Until Product sync tapped: "F-47 Checkout totals snoozed: back after Product sync, Nov 26" with Undo and a "Seen › Coming back 3" link to where it waits; the counts drop by one.
